Let me analyze this certificate.

It's an OIML Certificate:
- Number: R76/2006-A-NL1-19.28, Revision 1
- Scheme: A (stated "issued under scheme A")
- Project number: 2683261
- Page total: 2
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 20 December 2021 (revision 1 date); revision history says Initial 23-05-2019, Revision 1 20-12-2021. The date_issued likely 2021-12-20.
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1
- Address: Thijsseweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands
- Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt
- Phone: +31 88 6362332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl

Applicant and Manufacturer: Shanghai Teraoka Electronics Co., Ltd., No.6058 of Nan Ting Road, Ting Ling Town, Jin Shan District, Shanghai 201505, China

Certified type: Non-automatic weighing instrument (Indicator? It's a complete instrument — category "Non-automatic weighing instrument"). Type: SM-120.

Recommendation: R76, edition 2006, scheme A, accuracy class III.

Test reports:
- NMi-14200153-01, 16 May 2014, 39 pages
- NMi-14200358-01, 30 July 2014, 19 pages
- NMi-15200265-01, 8 May 2015, 25 pages
- NMi-1902238-01, 20 April 2018, 12 pages
- NMi-2371200-01, 23 May 2019, 24 pages
- NMi-2573473-01, 26 February 2021, 26 pages

Role: type_evaluation_report? They are OIML test reports. The schema says role: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. These are test reports supporting the type evaluation. I'll use "test_report" or "type_evaluation_report". The certificate says "tests and examinations provided in the associated OIML Reports". I'll use "type_evaluation_report" — hmm, they're referred to as "OIML Reports" / test reports. Let me use "test_report".

Revision history:
- "Initial" / 23-05-2019 / "-"
- "1" / 20-12-2021 / "Addition of new L6D type loadcell based on NMi-2573473-01 test report"

Revision should be string: "0"? The schema says revision (string, e.g. "0" not 0). The markdown says "Initial" — keep as "Initial"? Rule says revision string e.g. "0". The table says "Initial" so I'll use "Initial" and "1".

Characteristics:
- Accuracy class: (III) — that's in recommendation.accuracy_classes ["III"] too. Could also be type_level characteristic. I'll include in recommendation.
- Maximum capacity: 3 kg ≤ Max ≤ 300 kg → value {min: 3, max: 300}, unit "kg". Label: maximum_capacity.
- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 1 g → value {min: 1, max: null}, unit "g". Label: verification_scale_interval.
- Weighing ranges: Single interval, Multi-interval → value string "Single interval / Multi-interval" — it's a list of options. Could be a string. I'll make value: "Single interval or Multi-interval"? Better to keep string "Single interval, Multi-interval". Hmm. Maybe make it a characteristic with value as string. Or config axis? These are two configurations. Actually could be model/config... but simplest: type_level characteristic `weighing_ranges` with value string.
- Maximum number of scale intervals (one weighing range): n ≤ 6000 divisions → value {min: null, max: 6000}, unit "divisions". Label: max_scale_intervals_single_range.
- Maximum number of scale intervals (multi-interval): n ≤ 3000 divisions (per partial weighing range) → {min: null, max: 3000}, unit divisions. Label: max_scale_intervals_multi_interval.
- Maximum number of partial weighing ranges: 2 → value 2, unit null.
- Tare: "T ≤ -50% for instruments with one weighing range; T ≤ -Max₁ for multi-interval instruments" → config_level? This varies by configuration (single vs multi-interval). Could be config_level with axis "weighing_range_type". Values: condition "single interval" → "-50%", condition "multi-interval" → "-Max1". Let me use config_level:
  - attribute: tare_limit (negative portion)
  - axis: weighing_range_configuration
  - values: [{condition: "single interval (one weighing range)", value: {min: null, max: -50}, unit: "%"}, {condition: "multi-interval", value: "-Max1", unit: null}]
  Actually "T ≤ -50%" means tare ≤ -50% (subtractive tare down to 50% of Max). I'll structure as value {min: null, max: -50}, unit "%".
  For "T ≤ -Max₁": value string "-Max1".
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C.
- Power supply voltage: 220 V / 230 V / 240 V AC 50/60 Hz → This is a list of discrete voltage values: 220, 230, 240 V. Per rules, lists of values → model matrix? No — these are alternative supply voltages, not models. Rule 3 says split: voltage and frequency. Voltage is a list {220, 230, 240}. I could represent value as string "220/230/240"? The rules say numbers not strings, ranges become min/max. A discrete list isn't a range. Hmm. I'll set value: [220, 230, 240]? The schema shape says value: number | {min,max} | string. A list isn't allowed strictly. Options: use min 220 max 240 (it happens to be contiguous). Or value string "220 / 230 / 240". I think min/max is misleading-ish but acceptable; alternatively string. I'll use {min: 220, max: 240} with unit V. Actually a discrete list — could represent as string "220 / 230 / 240". Rule 2 says value must be number, min/max object, or string. For a discrete list, string seems safest but violates "numbers, not strings". Given contiguity, min/max 220–240 captures it. I'll go with {min: 220, max: 240}, unit "V".
  - Frequency: 50/60 Hz → {min: 50, max: 60}, unit "Hz".
  - power_supply_type: "AC".
- Application: "Intended to be used for direct sales to the public" → string.
- Software identification: "Version number: VR01.xx (xx = 00…99)" → string. Label: software_identification or software_version.

No footnotes. No model family (single type SM-120). No components... The revision mentions load cell L6D but not as component of certified type really — it says "Addition of new L6D type loadcell based on ... test report". It's part of the certified type's changes but the cert doesn't have components section. I won't add components since the certified type is a complete weighing instrument; but the L6D load cell could be a component. Hmm — rule 6: include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The revision history mentions "L6D type loadcell". That's a sub-assembly referenced. But it's in the revision change note, not a characteristic. I could add a component entry: role "load cell", type_designations ["L6D"]. It's a judgment call. It's mentioned as part of the type (revision 1 adds it). I think including it is defensible but risky. The characteristics table doesn't mention it. I'll omit components to avoid fabrication? Actually the text does name it: "Addition of new L6D type loadcell based on NMi-2573473-01 test report". This is a named sub-assembly. I'll include components: [{role: "load cell", type_designations: ["L6D"]}]. Hmm... The cert is for the instrument SM-120; the load cell is a component. I'll include it with alternatives null.

Actually, let me be careful: "L6D type loadcell" — this is likely a Teraoka/Digi load cell model. Including as component seems reasonable.
